newsitem.title: LATVIA: LITHUANIA - VILNIAUS SAYS INTEREST RATE FALL KEY.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - VILNIAUS SAYS INTEREST RATE FALL KEY.

text.p: Lithuania's Vilniaus Bank said one of the main priorities had to be getting the country's interest rates to fall to boost economic growth.
"The primary objective at the moment is to allow lending rates to fall to more sustainable levels," the bank said in its May report.

"But in March, the cost of new borrowing for many Lithuanian companies despite declining inflation went up by two percent and stood at 15 percent for short-term lending and rose by one percent month-on-month for long-term lending," the bank said.
"In a credit-driven economy, high rates of lending could wipe out economic growth," the bank warned.
"Things are complicated by the high value of the currency, as the litas is pegged to the dollar, which went up against the D-mark recently," the bank said.
The bank also said that the country's banking sector, hit by a severe crisis in late 1995, has shown signs of remarkable recovery but public confidence in commercial banks remains low.
It said that deposits at the end of 1996 were only $1.1 billion or 14.2 percent of gross domestic product (GDP).
"Keeping money under matresses instead of channeling it in into economic growth is a massive waste of resources," the bank said.
